openingPanels.title: Four different ways of holding a scene
purposes: Compare a focal figure, a pair, a sea scene and a night setting.
Keep recognisability separate from colour and repeated shapes.

openingPanels.title: The face and the field
purposes: Compare three treatments of a close figure with an uninterrupted colour field. Gold Marilyn shows one photograph-derived face. Recognition, subject and medium can distinguish the responses.

openingPanels.title: Close relationships and public company
purposes: Compare intimate care with figures sharing a public setting.
Two Cassatt works offer a limited within-artist contrast; subject and handling still differ.

openingPanels.title: Colour in objects and landscapes
purposes: Compare colour and space in three still-life treatments and an outdoor scene. A landscape response may depend on the figure, distance or handling.

openingPanels.title: Abstraction can be sparse or dense
purposes: Keep abstraction separate from visible density.
Compare geometric order with accumulating marks and rhythm.

openingPanels.title: An expressive head and bodily action
purposes: Compare Basquiat’s single worked-over head and Munch’s altered face with an explicit physical contest and a quieter figure. The ratings concern appeal.

openingPanels.title: How groups direct attention
purposes: Compare spatial and light cues in four group scenes. A visible exchange requires its own evidence.

openingPanels.title: What a scene leaves unexplained
purposes: Compare withheld faces, a sleeping figure with a lion, a blindfolded musician and an imagined act of making. Apparent meaning and any later note remain separate reports.

openingPanels.title: A room can organise a story or stay quiet
purposes: Compare elaborate interior encounters with a restrained inhabited room.
Keep surrounding space separate from the number of objects or secondary clues.

openingPanels.title: Focus and visual construction
purposes: See whether geometric edges or selective light and bodily action draw appeal in different treatments. These works also differ in subject, palette and handling.

openingPanels.title: Weather, scale and landscape
purposes: Compare natural settings through broken colour planes, expansive weather, a receding valley and layered winter activity. The variation makes landscape a more useful subject to test.

openingPanels.title: Story clues can accumulate or concentrate
purposes: Compare clues concentrated around a figure with distributed objects and incidents.
A dense scene and a symbolic subject need not be the same preference.

openingPanels.title: Dense stories and different kinds of tragedy
purposes: Compare dense storytelling in Bosch and Rivera, then two very different Goya scenes.
Crowded composition, physically fantastical imagery and depicted violence are distinct candidate explanations.
Report felt unease and willingness to return separately; neither is inferred from the subject.

openingPanels.title: Different amounts of space for an image to imply meaning
purposes: Compare a compact graphic figure with extensive scenes and gathered objects.
Documented symbolism remains context, not a visual score inferred from the title.

openingPanels.title: Action, tragedy and visual spectacle
purposes: Compare the tragic scenes of Guernica and Collective Suicide with nonviolent bodily action and illuminated spectacle.
Differences in palette, fragmentation, subject and historical knowledge remain competing explanations.

openingPanels.title: Night interiors and paired portraits
purposes: Compare The Night Café with Nighthawks for illuminated interiors, colour, handling and interpersonal clues.
Compare The Two Fridas with American Gothic for paired figures and visibly expressed symbolic connection.
Neither familiar artists nor multiple figures establish liking or an interest in interpersonal exchange.

openingPanels.title: Social scenes through different handling
purposes: Compare everyday group relationships across precise and altered treatment.
The paired admiration question asks about making separately from preference.

openingPanels.title: Precise edges across imagined and abstract forms
purposes: Compare meticulous imagined scenes with organic and geometric abstraction.
Clear edges remain common here, so precision is not treated as the opposite of abstraction.

comparisons.title: Constructed views
comparisons.purpose: Compare the continuity of a painted landscape and its window with Hockney’s divided poolside view.

comparisons.title: Space and the uncanny
comparisons.purpose: Cross far-off coast and island views with differences in impossible forms and visual focus.

comparisons.title: Treatment of a figure
comparisons.purpose: Compare what handling does to an emphatically posed figure. Subject, palette and genre also differ.

comparisons.title: Natural forms up close and in space
comparisons.purpose: Compare an enlarged flower with a garden whose vegetation forms a setting.

comparisons.title: Changed bodily proportions
comparisons.purpose: Compare a doubled figure with dense repeated pattern and one elongated figure in a spare setting.

comparisons.title: Different handling of depicted violence
comparisons.purpose: Compare a still aftermath with active struggle. Felt unease requires a separate report.

comparisons.title: Poses and social attention
comparisons.purpose: Compare deliberately posed figures with visible interactions in a gathering.

comparisons.title: Figures with animal forms
comparisons.purpose: Compare Chagall’s intersecting village imagery with Lam’s tightly interwoven forms.

comparisons.title: Framing a figure and its setting
comparisons.purpose: Compare a recognizable portrait quotation with a self-portrait placed between contrasting environments.

comparisons.title: Graphic line and repeated forms
comparisons.purpose: Compare a single close comic face and speech with a dense mural-like web of repeated graphic bodies.

comparisons.title: Colour and the organisation of a place
comparisons.purpose: Compare an interior reduced to a red field and a populated outdoor setting with independently legible parts.

comparisons.title: Groups under pressure
comparisons.purpose: Compare directed bodily action in two layered group scenes under different circumstances.

comparisons.title: Figure groups and bodily gesture
comparisons.purpose: Compare a staged foreground group with several dancers and distinct uses of gesture.

comparisons.title: Light and surface across views
comparisons.purpose: Compare Monet’s close architectural surface with the clearly divided expanses in Vallotton’s fields.
